entries.description: Value1 (X) is the native ability ID. Value2 (Y) is the flat AP-cost adjustment for that ability. It is added to the flat cost subtotal before the nonnegative clamp and general AP-cost multiplier, so it can add an AP cost to an ability with a zero base cost. Other ability cost rules still apply.

Description.value:

- Note: This can give AP costs to abilities that did not originally have one

entries.description: Value1 (X) selects the native HP, MP, or AP attribute. Value2 (Y) supplies the percentage rate. Rates for the ability's primary attribute are ignored; rates for each other attribute are added together. Additional resource damage is potential damage multiplied by that rate, divided by 100 with integer truncation. It uses potential damage before the target's resource cap, not the amount actually removed.

Description.value: X% of this ability's total damage is also dealt to the target's Y attribute, where Y is the target's HP, AP, or MP. Useful when creating abilities intended to damage more than one resource at once

entries.description: Value1 (X) adjusts the magical variance multiplier by (100 + X) / 100. Each modifier multiplies the accumulated multiplier by (100 + X), then divides by 100 with integer truncation. The result applies to magical abilities after additive variance adjustments.

Description.value: Multiplies Variance for Magical abilities by X%

entries.description: Value1 (X) adds to the accumulated steal bonus. For one available loot entry, the native chance calculation returns 100 * (base chance + bonus) / (100 + bonus), with integer truncation. A base chance of 20 and bonus of 50 gives 46%. Loot availability is a separate roll. The attempt also applies native luck and consecutive-failure handling. A total bonus of -100 is invalid because the divisor is zero.

Description.value: Increase steal success chance by X%

entries.description: Character growth, resting loadout totals, and supported combat arithmetic use the verified Windows PC 1.6.9 calculation package. The package records integer operations, rounding, modifier order, input requirements, and checks against compiled native methods. Combat calculations need explicit actor, target, ability, and battle context; a resting build preview does not simulate a complete encounter. Export the package from a Build or character calculation panel, or read the native calculation reference.
